Chapter 177: 0174 Puzzling Human Behavior

The airport, waiting hall.

Chen Guiliang looked at the text message he had just received, his mood a tangled mess.

Replying to Tao Xue would be like giving her hope, and the girl would only fall deeper.

But not replying felt wrong. After all, they were friends, and Chen Guiliang was also partners with her brother.

Besides, Chen Guiliang wasn't made of stone.

The way Tao Xue had hugged him and wept that day had both moved him and made his heart ache, and he couldn't bring himself to say any more harsh words.

It seemed he was starting to like Tao Xue.

But Bian Guanyue was also deeply devoted to him, even choosing to study at a school in Beijing specifically for him. And when Chen Guiliang was most desperate for money, she had given him the dowry her grandfather had saved for her before he passed away, several hundred thousand yuan, without even asking for an IOU.

How many girls could do something like that?

"Senior, are you on the plane yet? Be safe." This was the text from Tao Xue.

After agonizing for a long time, Chen Guiliang replied: "Still at the airport."

Tao Xue replied in seconds: "The school is so annoying. I just got home a day ago, and now they're saying we have to have makeup classes. Some of our classmates from the countryside don't have phones or internet, so the school is even making students who live in towns go and notify them."

"Try to look at it from another angle. The school administration must have the biggest headache. A perfectly normal summer makeup session has turned into such a hassle," Chen Guiliang replied.

"Haha, that's true."

As they were chatting, another text came from Bian Guanyue: "I learned how to make sweet and sour pork ribs from my grandpa. I'll make them for you next time."

Chen Guiliang held his forehead. Nothing had happened between him and Tao Xue, and he hadn't made any moves on her. He had even told her he was already in a relationship, hoping she would back off. But at this moment, he felt like a scumbag.

Do I have a scumbag constitution?

I was single until I was thirty in my past life!

"I'm sure it will be delicious," Chen Guiliang replied casually.

Another text came from Tao Xue: "Li Yuchun posted a photo on Kaixinwang today. A lot of people liked it, I did too."

"I prefer Zhou Bichang," Chen Guiliang quickly replied.

Then another message came from Bian Guanyue...

Chen Guiliang went from his initial entanglement to a gradual numbness, mechanically carrying on a two-way conversation.

How the hell was he supposed to sort out this three-person relationship?

Han Han has two women, and they can even coexist harmoniously. How did that guy do it?

Chen Guiliang really wanted to ask Han Han for advice, mainly because he had no experience in this area.

"Wei-ge, have you ever been in a relationship?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Yang Shuo was traveling with Chen Guiliang this time. He shook his head and said, "I've never even held a girl's hand."

Sigh, asking the blind for directions.

Chen Guiliang texted Li Xunhuan: "You have Han Han's phone number, right? Please send it to me."

Li Xunhuan quickly sent the number over.

Chen Guiliang began a three-way conversation: "Hello, I'm Chen Guiliang."

Han Han: "Hello."

"Pardon my asking, but how do you handle a relationship with two girls at the same time?"

"Wei-shi said you have several girlfriends. I'd like to ask for your advice."

"I like them, and they like me. It's that simple."

"How do you all get along?"

"I don't lie to them. I'm sincere with all of them."

"So you have a clear conscience?"

"Right."

"Impressive."

Chen Guiliang stopped chatting with this scumbag and continued his two-way conversation with Bian Guanyue and Tao Xue.

But a few minutes later, another text came from Han Han: "Take care."

Chen Guiliang asked curiously: "Have you crashed and burned before?"

Han Han didn't reply again.

Yang Shuo, sitting beside him, saw Chen Guiliang typing furiously on his phone, having texted for more than ten minutes. He sighed with emotion inwardly: Being a boss is so busy. If you have to handle work like this every day, your fingers must get worn out.

Finally, the painful yet pleasant chat ended with the sentence "I'm boarding now."

It was Yang Shuo's first time on a plane, and also his first time in a major international metropolis—the Magic City.

He found everything novel.

But he managed to appear calm, carefully observing everything around him.

"What are we here for?" Yang Shuo asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "To attend an event. Its English name is Chinajoy, and the Chinese name is China Digital Entertainment Expo & Conference."

"Oh." Yang Shuo was completely clueless.

Chen Guiliang said, "You can start by helping with odd jobs, like setting up the booth, handing out flyers, and so on. If you don't understand something, just ask. There are many things you have to learn slowly."

This year's Chinajoy would last for three days: the first day for industry exchange, the second for public experience, and the third for a gamer carnival.

Chen Guiliang was here this time to promote *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*, hoping to attract more media attention while also seeking cooperation with distributors—prepaid card distributors, physical card distributors, and Hong Kong and Taiwan online game distributors.

"Boss!"

"Mr. Chen!"

Chen Guiliang took Yang Shuo straight to the hotel.

The team was already waiting for him.

There were two people in charge.

One was Liang Bin, a business development specialist from Game Science, responsible for making initial contact with distributors while Chen Guiliang attended the summit forum.

The other was Tian Yongzhe, an offline event specialist borrowed from ByteDance, responsible for setting up the booth, player demos, cosplay performances, and so on.

Chen Guiliang's former team leader from his past life, Qu Guohao, had been transferred over to be Tian Yongzhe's deputy this time.

The reason Qu Guohao wasn't in charge was that Tian Yongzhe had already done the preliminary planning, so there was no need for a last-minute change.

In addition, the staff members who came along would also double as cosplayers.

Yang Shuo followed them into the elevator and up the stairs. In the hallway leading to the guest rooms, he saw a group of demons and monsters.

One person was wearing a yellow Taoist robe and a Daoist topknot wig, pointing his finger forward: "The Blue Sky is dead, the Yellow Sky shall rise!"

Across from him stood another person, wearing a bull's head and holding a giant axe, shouting, "The Earth Mother is with you... Damn, no momentum. For the glory of the Horde!"

Behind these two were other men and women, all dressed in strange costumes.

Yang Shuo was utterly shocked, seeing such a scene for the first time: "Are they shooting a movie?"

"It's just like when you used to pretend to be Guo Jing as a kid, but these are all game characters," Chen Guiliang explained.

Yang Shuo understood instantly.

Chen Guiliang asked the tauren, "Are you guys from The9?"

"Yeah, you play *World of Warcraft* too?" the tauren asked back.

"I have."

Chen Guiliang looked at the Jaina behind the tauren. Although she was average-looking, her chest was even more revealing than in the game.

He then looked at the Zhen Ji cosplayed by Xu Fengyin. She was actually less revealing than Jaina.

The costume was too conservative!

"Boss, what do you think of our cosplay?" Cao Cao asked, flicking his cape.

"Are you Chen Di?"

"Yes."

"Damn, with the beard and the helmet, I almost didn't recognize you."

The *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* cosplayers from Game Science were all company employees moonlighting. When they weren't performing on stage, they had to handle other event duties.

Since Game Science was short on staff, several had been borrowed from ByteDance.

Chen Guiliang asked, "How did you guys get into a standoff with the Warcraft crew?"

Chen Di, who was cosplaying Cao Cao, said, "They're also The9 employees moonlighting. We ran into them on the same hotel floor, so we all changed into our gear to spar a little."

Chen Guiliang had them change out of their strange costumes and called everyone for a meeting to discuss the details of the next three days' activities.

The next day.

Chen Guiliang led his team to the convention center and saw many "acquaintances."

Of course, he knew these "acquaintances," but they didn't necessarily know him.

The opening ceremony lasted for half an hour, with speeches from leaders of the GAPP and the Magic City respectively.

After that, Chen Guiliang went to attend the summit forum.

The others went to do other things.

Chen Guiliang was a small fry in the industry. The only ones who could give speeches on stage were people like Chen Tianqiao and Ding Sanshi. Even Lei Bus had to sit obediently below and listen to them brag.

Fortunately, the bragging didn't last long, and it was followed by roundtable discussions, where guests would exchange ideas in groups.

Sitting at the same table as Chen Guiliang were Park Heon-joo from Ourgame, a Korean; Wang Zijie from 9you; Yang Jin from GZTC; Zhang Chun from Object Software; and Liu Kun from Pixel Soft.

With the exception of Ourgame, they were all game companies that were slightly lacking in strength but had shown some impressive results.

GZTC once had its moment of glory, having been the distributor for *The Legend of Mir 3*.

9you was the distributor for *Audition Online*, which was extremely popular at the time.

As early as two years ago, Ourgame had over 200 million registered users and 15 million monthly active users, with servers in China, the US, Japan, and South Korea. This was the common enemy of Game Science Interactive and QQ Games!

Park Heon-joo looked a bit displeased. He felt he should be sitting at the same table as Chen Tianqiao and Ding Sanshi.

Liu Kun knew Chen Guiliang, and their companies had even lent each other programmers. "Mr. Chen, we meet again."

"Yes, it must be fate," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Zhang Chun from Object Software handed out business cards to everyone. When he got to Chen Guiliang, he said, "Mr. Chen, I've long heard of your name. *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* has been making quite a splash this year."

"Likewise, likewise," Chen Guiliang said. "I'm a big fan of *Tianjiao*."

The five Chinese people at the table exchanged business cards and also gave one to the Korean.

Chen Guiliang sat next to Yang Jin from GZTC and asked in a low voice, "Isn't the CEO of Ourgame Bao Yueqiao? Even if not, they could have sent another executive. What's the deal with sending a Korean as a representative?"

Yang Jin smiled, "The Koreans are in the middle of a power grab."

Chen Guiliang couldn't understand. A power grab within the company was one thing. But to fight over attending an event, wasn't that just making a fool of themselves in public?

Ourgame, a giant just two years ago, had already been severely weakened just one year after being acquired by the Koreans.

The Korean headquarters didn't trust the Chinese, so they replaced all the cadres two levels below the general manager and department heads at Ourgame with Koreans sent from headquarters. This led to a breakdown in effective communication between Chinese executives and lower-level employees.

These Korean mid-level managers also forced the Korean way of doing things onto China, causing a massive loss of Ourgame users. Whenever a dispute arose, they would complain to headquarters, which led to the constant replacement of Chinese executives.

This kind of absurd mismanagement would continue for several years.

One Korean team would go back to Korea, only for a second to be sent over. This would happen four or five times, until Ourgame was almost run into the ground before they stopped.

The moderator was arranged by the event organizer: "Good morning, gentlemen. Our first topic is the current difficulties in China's online gaming industry and how to break through them."

Yang Jin was the first to state his view. He believed there were too many hacks and private servers, and that computer hardware and internet speeds were also major limitations. He went on about how to develop, blah blah blah.

Zhang Chun was about to speak next, but the Korean cut in.

The Korean, named Park Heon-joo, could actually speak Chinese: "The biggest difficulty for China's online games is that the Chinese don't understand the internet. In Korea, our casual game platforms are all web-based, without any cumbersome game clients. This is because Korean webpages are very clean and can run driver plugins. But these plugins are often mistaken for malware by Chinese antivirus software, making it impossible to run web games in China!"

"The Chinese people are very stupid; they have no idea how to make games. Your most popular online games all rely on being agents for Korean games. I believe that if the Chinese online gaming industry wants to develop healthily, it should fully learn from Korea, from management models to game mechanics. Chinese game companies should also hire Koreans as executives."

The other five people at the table, plus the moderator for this table, were all dumbfounded by the Korean's speech.

Was this guy insane?

Chen Guiliang had always thought that such brain-dead words and actions could only appear in trashy, amateurish web novels.

Because it defied logic; no normal person would do such a thing.

He never expected to encounter it in reality today.

You freaking snatched the right to represent Ourgame at this event from its Chinese founder. And the first thing you do is offend your peers. What are you trying to achieve?

Just to vent your dissatisfaction?

It was simply baffling.

Park Heon-joo's thinking was actually very simple. He was unhappy about being placed at this table.

Moreover, back at the Korean headquarters, he had to be a yes-man, but in China, he could be a king at Ourgame. A few months of kingly treatment had inflated his ego.

His outrageous speech was, in fact, exactly what Park Heon-joo truly thought!

The few Chinese people present didn't even feel angry; their minds were just filled with bewilderment. Everyone was thinking: What is wrong with this guy?

The moderator reminded him, "Mr. Park, please watch your wording."

"I'm just telling the truth," Park Heon-joo continued to express his dissatisfaction. "Also, I want to protest to the organizers. Ourgame is China's largest casual gaming platform. Being placed at this table does not match my status."

The moderator said, "If you have an issue with the event arrangements, you can file a complaint afterward. Please do not cause a disruption now."

"Hey, Brother Bàng," Chen Guiliang called out.

Park Heon-joo was talking to the moderator and turned his head to look at Chen Guiliang upon hearing this.

Chen Guiliang smiled and raised his middle finger.

"Hahaha!"

All the Chinese people at the table burst out laughing, even the moderator chuckled.

(End of this chapter)
